name: Screen print
how: Ink is pushed through a fine mesh screen onto the fabric. One screen is prepared per colour in the design.
bestFor: Bulk runs with a small number of flat colours
strengths: Lowest per-piece cost once quantity rises
Strong, opaque colour on dark fabric

name: DTF (direct to film)
how: The design is printed onto a transfer film, coated with adhesive powder, then heat-pressed onto the garment.
bestFor: Small runs and complex multi-colour artwork
limits: Slight surface feel where ink sits
Large solid areas can feel heavy

name: DTG (direct to garment)
how: Ink is jetted straight into the fabric by a specialised printer, much like an inkjet printing onto cloth.
bestFor: Photographic artwork where a soft hand feel matters
limits: Dark garments need a pre-treat and white underbase

name: Embroidery
how: Artwork is digitised into a stitch file, then sewn into the fabric with thread.
bestFor: Logos on polos, caps and workwear
limits: Cannot reproduce gradients or fine text
Adds weight and stiffness on light fabric

name: Sublimation
how: Under heat, dye converts to gas and bonds into polyester fibre, becoming part of the fabric itself.
strengths: Individual names and numbers cost nothing extra
limits: Polyester only — will not work on cotton
Whole panel must be printed before assembly
